subject: BrightMart: index cutover logistics, backfill cadence & rerank smoke tests

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team at BrightMart is excited to move forward with Redwood for semantic search and a reranker layer. Before we lock an onboarding start date we have a few operational questions so we can scope procurement and engineering effort:

- Index backfill: our catalog is ~120M text chunks (HTML snippets + metadata). What’s a recommended backfill cadence (daily incremental vs one-shot bulk) and an expected time-to-complete for a cold backfill?
- Vector store options: we prefer a managed vector DB but are open to self-hosting. Can you summarize the tradeoffs you see (throughput, snapshot/restore, multi-region)?
- Rerank evaluation: we need acceptance criteria. What sample sizes and metrics should we run for MRR/NDCG regression risk?
- Downtime/consistency: will the cutover require read-only windows for the existing search service?

Claire — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and a proposed operational plan below.

High-level recommendations
- Backfill approach: staged bulk backfill + daily incremental. For a catalog at ~120M chunks we typically do a week-long cold backfill (parallel workers, shard-by-namespace) and then switch to 1x/day incremental sync. This lowers peak resource costs and makes rollback easier.
- Vector store tradeoffs: managed stores (Pinecone/VectorDB SaaS) give easiest ops and multi-region replication; self-hosted (Milvus/Weaviate) gives cost control and more direct access for snapshots. Redwood’s vector adapter layer supports both; we recommend managed for initial go-live and evaluate self-hosting in Q4 if needed.
- Rerank evals: target ~2k labeled queries for an initial sanity run; evaluate MRR and NDCG@10 plus precision@1. If you have existing relevance judgments we can bootstrap.
- Cutover window: we can avoid full downtime with a blue/green-style switch — read-only for writes to the old index for no more than 10 minutes during final validation (depends on backfill completion).

Proposed next steps (technical call recommended)
1) 45-min technical sync (SRE + search eng + Redwood CS) — proposed Wed 2026-08-11 11:00 PT
2) Backfill estimation run: Redwood runs a dry run on a 5% sample and provides wall-clock and cost estimate
3) Rerank smoke tests: Redwood provides an evaluation template and sample scripts; BrightMart provides 2k sample queries
4) Cutover rehearsal on staging, then 1-day production cutover with canary traffic at 5/25/100%

I’ll attach the rough schedule and owner assignments after we confirm the sync.

— Hannah

Claire / team — adding an implementation checklist and notes from the engineering perspective. See inline and attached rerank_eval_template.xlsx for the evaluation spreadsheet.

- Backfill execution notes:
  * Recommended workers: start with 200 parallel workers (k8s pods) throttled by vector DB write capacity; expect ~3–5TB of vector data written depending on dims/quantization.
  * Snapshot strategy: keep hourly checkpoints during backfill; retain 7 days for rollback.
  * Throttling: schedule heavy writes during off-peak hours (00:00–06:00 local).

- Vector DB tradeoffs (short):
  * Managed (fast start): automatic scaling, built-in replication + backups; higher IO cost; limited kernel-level tuning.
  * Self-hosted (control): lower long-term cost for heavy write workloads, must manage compaction and shard placement, but better for on-prem/regulatory requirements.

- Rerank smoke tests & acceptance criteria:
  * Sample size: 2,000 labeled queries (mix of navigational, transactional, long-tail)
  * Metrics: MRR, NDCG@10, precision@1, latency P95 of reranker (<120ms target)
  * Regression threshold: no more than 2% drop in MRR or 0.03 absolute NDCG drop vs baseline for canary traffic; otherwise auto-roll back.

Action items for brightmart before the sync:
- Share 2k sample queries + labels (CSV or Google Sheet)
- Share preferred vector DB vendor or if you want Redwood-managed store
- Provide a test account with representative data (5% sample)

Monica

Claire / team — attaching a concise runbook and an initial cost estimate for the dry run. High-level tech notes:

- Backfill steps (summary):
  1) Transform raw catalog -> tokenized/cleaned chunks (mapreduce jobs)
  2) Generate embeddings in parallel (batch size 512, mixed-precision)
  3) Bulk write to vector store with per-shard concurrency
  4) Snapshot and run verification queries (checksum+sample recall)

- Time estimate (5% sample dry run):
  * Embedding generation: ~4 hours using 8xA100 equivalent nodes
  * Bulk write: ~2.5 hours to managed vector store at recommended write QPS
  * Verification: ~30–45 minutes

- Quantization & storage: using int8 + PQ reduces raw vector storage by ~3–4x; we recommend enabling quantization for long-term storage after verifying rerank quality on the canary.

Attachments: backfill_runbook.md, estimated_costs.csv

If the team approves the Wed sync Hannah suggested, I’ll bring SRE and the embeddings infra lead to walk through the runbook.

— Priyom
